messages:
incident-bot: paging on-call for elevated 5xx + streaming disconnects in us-west-edge — error rate spike from 0.2% to ~6% across streaming endpoints. auto-detected 3377778885.

mike_oncall: acked — I'm on it, joining. Anyone seen recent deploys to edge gateway in the last 30m? @sara_dev @jia_ops

sara_dev: saw a small nginx config tweak 22m ago (keepalive tweaks) rolled with 2-minute canary. I pushed the change but saw no obvious red flags in canary logs.

jia_ops: i'm pulling gateway logs now, looks like lots of upstream resets and chunked-encoding truncated frames: `upstream prematurely closed connection` and `client canceled` entries. sample: `2026-03-15T18:04:12Z ERROR http: upstream prematurely closed connection (peer reset) for request /v1/stream`

leo_platform: metric snapshot from edge: 5xx spike concentrated on streaming fanout routes (/v1/stream, /v1/chat/streams). p95 latency for initial chunk up from 80ms -> 420ms. Backend (pods) cpu OK. Queue length on the gateway fanout queue rising.

mike_oncall: ok, priority: stop customer impact. Quick ideas: 1) throttle or drop large fanout requests, 2) route streaming to degraded fallback instance set (no batching), 3) scale gateway replicas / restart. Which is fastest?

tara_support: we already have two customers reporting partial responses and reconnect loops. One on higher tier — flagging for possible SLA.

sara_dev: we can enable fallback routing to the non-batching path immediately (config flag). That will reduce concurrency on KV cache and reduce long-lived connections. Patching now: `PATCH /admin/route-config` with body `{ "stream_fanout_mode": "fallback" }`.

jia_ops: doing the patch. Applying to us-west-edge...

ops-runbook-bot: runbook step triggered: STREAM-1 > Activate fallback routing; Notify customers; Increase gateway replicas if error persists.

jia_ops: fallback applied to 75% of traffic at 18:07:33, monitoring.

leo_platform: error rate dropped from 6.1% -> 2.5% after fallback. Still elevated vs baseline. seeing chunk truncation errors decrease but timeouts still present for some streams: `client canceled` and `recv timeout` on connections that lasted >20s.

mike_oncall: can we isolate whether it's upstream (model runtime) closing or edge dropping? Grab tcpdump on gateway to inspect RSTs and Content-Length/chunked semantics.

jia_ops: tcpdump shows repeated FIN+ACK from upstream (runtime) after ~18s on problematic requests. upstream logs show `OOM` messages in one runtime shard (shard-7) around 18:02.

sara_dev: shard-7 had a memory regression after the recent quantization library bump. It may lead to process restarts and mid-stream closures. I can spin up extra replicas for shard-7 and evict old ones.

leo_platform: I've started a hotfix job: scale shard-7 by +3 replicas (manual) and add a pod anti-affinity to spread load. Triggered at 18:12.

mike_oncall: good. while scaling, we should reduce simultaneous fanout per-request to limit downstream concurrency. Suggest per-request fanout cap = 8. Can we apply in gateway config?

jia_ops: applying `max_fanout_per_request: 8` to us-west-edge and us-west-worker pool at 18:14.

tara_support: customer update: sent initial note at 18:15 — affected sessions may see reconnects; we are investigating and will update in 30m.

ops-runbook-bot: runbook step: SCALE-RUNTIME > increased shard-7 replicas; MONITOR for 10m.

leo_platform: after scaling shard-7 + fanout cap + fallback routing, 5xx rate is down to 0.7% and latency p95 back to ~120ms. chunk truncation errors are rare.

mike_oncall: excellent. mark mitigation success for live triage. Next: create incident ticket, note RCA candidates (quant-lib regression -> memory ctrl issues under fanout), and schedule postmortem.

sara_dev: putting a revert patch to quantization lib under review (small change) — i'll hold until we stabilize, but ready to rollback if we see restarts again.

jia_ops: scheduling a rolling restart of remaining old runtime pods to ensure no hung processes at 18:25.

mike_oncall: handoff to night on-call in 45m. @leo_platform pls prepare a short handoff summary: what to watch, commands to remediate, and where to find logs.

leo_platform: handoff summary drafted and uploaded to /incidents/3377778888/artifacts — includes grafana snapshots, example tcpdump snippets, and commands:```bash
# scale runtime shard
kubectl scale deployment/runtime-shard-7 --replicas=5 -n prod
# fallback routing (if needed)
curl -s -X PATCH $ADMIN_URL/route-config -d '{"stream_fanout_mode":"fallback"}'
# cap fanout
kubectl apply -f - <<EOF
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: gateway-config
data:
  max_fanout_per_request: "8"
EOF
```

tara_support: i've notified the two reporting customers with ETA 45m and will keep support channel updated.

mike_oncall: status: mitigation in place, customer-impact reduced, ready for detailed RCA. Closing live triage but keeping incident open for postmortem. If errors resurge, page on-call with high urgency. :white_check_mark:

incident-bot: Incident update: P1 -> mitigated, severity lowered. Incident ticket created: INC-2026-3377. Postmortem owner assigned: sara_dev.

mike_oncall: thanks team — handing off to night on-call at 19:00. If anyone sees residual client cancels correlated with long-lived streams, escalate immediately.

--- end of thread ---
